Problem stem: Using the $\epsilon$-$\delta$ definition, explain why $\lim_{x \to 3} (2x + 1) = 7$. Specifically, given an arbitrary $\epsilon > 0$, find a suitable $\delta$.
Canonical answer: Choose $\delta = \epsilon/2$. Then $0 < |x - 3| < \delta$ implies $|2x + 1 - 7| = 2|x - 3| < 2(\epsilon/2) = \epsilon$.
Student answer: You just plug in x = 3 and get 7 so the limit is 7
